groups.passage: The Nobel Peace Center is located in an old train station building close to the Oslo City Hall and overlooking the harbor. It was officially opened on June 11, 2005 as part of the celebrations to [[11]] Norway’s centenary as an independent country. It is a center where you can experience and learn about the various Nobel Peace Prize Laureates and their activities [[12]] the remarkable history of Alfred Nobel, the founder of the Nobel Prize. In addition, it serves as a meeting place where exhibits, discussions, and reflections [[13]] to war, peace, and conflict resolution are in focus. The Center combines exhibits and films with digital communication and interactive installations and has already received attention for its use of state-of-the-art technology. Visitors are welcome to experience the Center [[14]] or join a guided tour. Since its opening, the Nobel Peace Center has been educating, inspiring and entertaining its visitors [[15]] exhibitions, activities, lectures, and cultural events. The Center is financed by private and public institutions.

groups.passage:
Alan Turing was one of the leading scientific geniuses of the 20th century. Many scholars consider him the father of modern computer science. He was also the man who cracked the [[16]] uncrackable Enigma code used by Nazi Germany. His code-breaking turned the tide of World War II and helped save two million lives. Nevertheless, [[17]] people have even heard his name.
Turing displayed signs of high intelligence in math and science at a young age. By the time he was 23, he had already come up with the idea of what [[18]] the modern computer—the Turing machine. Today, Turing machines are still used in theoretical computation. He also proposed the now famous Turing test, used to determine whether a computer exhibits intelligent behavior equivalent to that of a human.
The postwar era, however, was a disaster for Turing. He was gay, which was then a crime in Britain. [[19]] being hailed as one of the crucial figures in defeating the Nazis, Turing was convicted of “gross indecency.” This [[20]] drove him to commit suicide in 1954, at the age of 41. Nearly 60 years after his death, Queen Elizabeth II granted Turing a formal pardon for his conviction, upon an online petition signed by prominent scientists and technology leaders around the world.

tags.topic: Alan Turing, code-breaker and father of computer science

groups.passage:
The Taiwanese puppet show (“Budaixi”) is a distinguished form of performing arts in Taiwan. Although basically hand puppets, the [[21]] appear as complete forms, with hands and feet, on an elaborately decorated stage.
The puppet performance is typically [[22]] by a small orchestra. The backstage music is directed by the drum player. The drummer needs to pay attention to what is going on in the plot and follow the rhythm of the characters. He also uses the drum to [[23]] the other musicians. There are generally around four to five musicians who perform the backstage music. The form of music used is often associated with various performance [[24]], including acrobatics and skills like window-jumping, stage movement, and fighting. Sometimes unusual animal puppets also appear on stage for extra [[25]], especially for children in the audience.
In general, a show needs two performers. The main performer is generally the chief or [[26]] of the troupe. He is the one in charge of the whole show, manipulating the main puppets, singing, and narrating. The [[27]] performer manipulates the puppets to coordinate with the main performer. He also changes the costumes of the puppets, and takes care of the stage. The relationship between the main performer and his partner is one of master and apprentice. Frequently, the master trains his sons to eventually [[28]] him as puppet masters.
Budaixi troupes are often hired to perform at festivals held in honor of local gods, and on happy [[29]] such as weddings, births, and promotions. The main purpose of Budaixi is to [[30]] and offer thanks to the deities. The shows also serve as a popular means of folk entertainment.

groups.passage:
Eccentrics are people who have an unusual or odd personality, set of beliefs, or behavior pattern. They may or may not comprehend the standards for normal behavior in their culture. They simply don’t care about the society’s disapproval of their habits or beliefs.
Once considered socially unacceptable, eccentric people have been found to possess some positive characteristics. [[31]] They often have more curiosity about the world and, in many cases, are contentedly obsessed by hobbies and interests. [[32]] They live in a world of their own and do not worry about what others think of them. So they are usually less restricted and therefore more carefree in forming new ideas.
[[33]] Statistics show they visit their doctors less—about once in eight to nine years, which is 20 times less than the average person. This could be partly due to their innate traits such as humor and happiness. [[34]] This may explain why eccentrics are, on the whole, healthier.
Psychologists therefore suggest that we pay attention to those who do not conform. It could be our aunt who has been raising pet lizards. [[35]] Their crazy hobby or strange sense of humor is what keeps them going. Eccentric people may seem odd, but they will likely live a happier and healthier life because they enjoy what they are doing. In fact, many of history’s most brilliant minds have displayed some unusual behaviors and habits.

groups.passage:
All pop artists like to say that they owe their success to their fans. In the case of British band SVM, it’s indeed true. The band is currently recording songs because 358 fans contributed the £100,000 needed for the project. The arrangement came via MMC, an online record label that uses Web-based, social-network-style “crowd-funding” to finance its acts.
Here’s how it works: MMC posts demos and videos of 10 artists on its website, and users are invited to invest from £10 to £1,000 in the ones they most enjoy or think are most likely to become popular. Once an act reaches £100,000, the financing process is completed, and the money is used to pay for recording and possibly a concert tour. Profits from resulting music sales, concerts, and merchandise are split three ways: investors get to divide 40%; another 40% goes to MMC; the artist pockets 20%. The payoff for investors can be big. One fan in France who contributed £4,250 got his money back 22 times over.
Crowd-funding musical acts is not new. But MMC takes the concept to another level. First of all, investors can get cash rather than just goodies like free downloads or tickets. Also, MMC is a record label. It has the means to get its music distributed around the world and to market artists effectively. “Artists need professional support,” says the CEO of MMC’s international division.
While digital technology and the Net have created a do-it-yourself boom among musicians, success is still a long shot. Out of the 20,000 records released in the U.S. in 2009, only 14 DIY acts made it to the Top 200. Also, with less revenue from recorded music, music companies have become less likely to take risks, which has led to fewer artists receiving funding. The crowd-funding model, however, allows for more records to be made by spreading risk among hundreds of backers. And the social-network aspect of the site helps expand fan bases; that is, investors become a promotional army.

groups.passage:
Fabergé eggs are jeweled eggs that were made by the famous Russian jeweler, the House of Fabergé, from 1885 to 1917. The eggs were made of valuable metals or stones coated with beautiful colors and decorated with precious jewels.
The first Fabergé egg was crafted for Tsar Alexander III, who gave his wife, the Empress Maria Fedorovna, an Easter egg to celebrate their 20th wedding anniversary. He placed an order with a young jeweler, Peter Carl Fabergé, whose beautiful creations had caught Maria’s eye earlier. On Easter morning of 1885, what appeared to be a simple enameled egg was delivered to the palace. But to the delight of the Empress, the egg opened to a golden yolk; within the yolk was a golden hen; and concealed within the hen was a diamond miniature of the royal crown and a tiny ruby egg. Unfortunately, the last two surprises are now lost to history.
Empress Maria was so delighted by this gift that Alexander appointed Fabergé a “goldsmith by special appointment to the Imperial Crown.” The Tsar also asked Fabergé to make an Easter egg every year. The requirements were straightforward: Each egg must be unique, and each must contain a pleasant surprise. With excellent craftsmanship and an inventive spirit, Peter Fabergé and his successors repeatedly met the challenge. The House of Fabergé made approximately 50 Imperial Easter Eggs for Tsar Alexander III and his son Nicholas II until 1917, when the Russian revolution broke out.
Today, the term “Fabergé eggs” has become a synonym of luxury and the eggs are regarded as masterpieces of the jeweler’s art. More significantly, perhaps, they serve as reminders of the last Russian imperial family.

groups.passage:
Spider webs are one of the most fascinating examples of animal architecture. The most beautiful and structurally ordered are the orb webs. The main function of the web is to intercept and hold flying prey, such as flies, bees and other insects, long enough for the spider to catch them. In order to do so, the threads of the web have to withstand the impact forces from large and heavy prey as well as environmental forces from wind and rain for at least a day in most cases.
The orb web is found to have two main characteristics. The first is its geometry, which consists of an outer frame and a central part from which threads radiate outward. Enclosed in the frame are capture spirals winding round and round from the web center out to the frame. The whole web is in tension and held in place by anchor threads, which connect the frame to the surrounding vegetation or objects. The second and perhaps most important characteristic is the material with which it is built. Spider silk is a kind of natural composite that gives this lightweight fiber a tensile strength comparable to that of steel, while at the same time making it very elastic. Two types of silk threads are used in the web. One is highly elastic and can stretch to almost twice its original length before breaking and, for most types of spiders, is covered in glue. This type is used in the capture spiral for catching and holding prey. The other is stiffer and stronger, and is used for the radius, frames and anchor threads, which allows the web to withstand prey impact and to keep its structural strength through a wide range of environmental conditions.

groups.passage:
Scientists are trying to genetically modify the world in which we live. They are even trying to wipe out diseases via genetic modification. For example, researchers have tried to engineer mosquitoes to kill malaria parasites. The malaria parasite is carried by the female Anopheles mosquito. When transmitted to a human, the parasite travels first to the liver and then on to the bloodstream, where it reproduces and destroys red blood cells. An estimated 250 million people suffer from malaria each year, and about one million die—many of them children. There are currently no effective or approved malaria vaccines.
To “kill” malaria, scientists are genetically modifying a bacterium in mosquitoes so that it releases toxic compounds. These compounds are not harmful to humans or the mosquito itself, but they do kill off the malaria parasite, making the mosquito incapable of infecting humans with malaria.
Despite this achievement, scientists are faced with the challenge of giving the modified mosquitoes a competitive advantage so that they can eventually replace the wild population. Complete blockage of the malaria parasite is very important. If some of the parasites slip through the mechanism, then the next generation will likely become resistant to it. And if that happens, the scientists are back where they started.
Another challenge for scientists is to gain public approval for this genetic modification regarding mosquitoes and malaria control. Environmental activists have raised concerns about the release of genetically engineered organisms without any clear knowledge of their long-term effect on ecosystems and human health. There is still a long way to go before genetic modification techniques are put to use in disease control.

options.D: Genetic engineering looks promising in reducing malaria, though there may be unknown consequences.

sections.title: 二、英文作文（占20分）
sections.instructions:
說明︰1.依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。
2.文長至少120個單詞（words）。

figures.label: 兩項新科技產品說明框
figures.description: 提示下方並排兩個說明框（左右各一），每個框的上緣是一個橢圓形標題泡泡，下方方框寫功能說明。左框：橢圓內寫「產品一：隱形披風（invisibility cloak）」，旁邊畫著一件帶兜帽的披風小圖示；方框內文字「穿上後頓時隱形，旁人看不到你的存在；同時，隱形披風會保護你，讓你水火不侵。」右框：橢圓內寫「產品二：智慧型眼鏡（smart glasses）」，旁邊畫著一副眼鏡小圖示；方框內文字「具有掃瞄透視功能，戴上後即能看到障礙物後方的生物；同時能完整紀錄你所經歷過的場景。」框內文字已逐字收在題目 stem。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem:
提示︰以下有兩項即將上市之新科技產品：
產品一：隱形披風（invisibility cloak）
穿上後頓時隱形，旁人看不到你的存在；同時，隱形披風會保護你，讓你水火不侵。
產品二：智慧型眼鏡（smart glasses）
具有掃瞄透視功能，戴上後即能看到障礙物後方的生物；同時能完整紀錄你所經歷過的場景。
如果你有機會獲贈其中一項產品，你會選擇哪一項？請以此為主題，寫一篇至少 120 個單詞的英文作文。文分兩段，第一段說明你的選擇及理由，並舉例說明你將如何使用這項產品。第二段說明你不選擇另一項產品的理由及該項產品可能衍生的問題。
questions.scoring_notes:
（本卷沒有公布評分原則；以下為同時公告之指考英文考科考試說明 other-1.pdf 所列，適用於英文作文的分項式評分標準。）
英文作文分項式評分標準（等級：優／可／差／劣）
內容：優（5-4分）＝主題（句）清楚切題，並有具體、完整的相關細節支持。／可（3分）＝主題不夠清楚或突顯，部分相關敘述發展不全。／差（2-1分）＝主題不明，大部分相關敘述發展不全或與主題無關。／劣（0分）＝文不對題或沒寫（凡文不對題或沒寫者，其他各項均以零分計算）。
組織：優（5-4分）＝重點分明，有開頭、發展、結尾，前後連貫，轉承語使用得當。／可（3分）＝重點安排不妥，前後發展比例與轉承語使用欠妥。／差（2-1分）＝重點不明、前後不連貫。／劣（0分）＝全文毫無組織或未按提示寫作。
文法、句構：優（5-4分）＝全文幾無文法、格式、標點錯誤，文句結構富變化。／可（3分）＝文法、格式、標點錯誤少，且未影響文意之表達。／差（2-1分）＝文法、格式、標點錯誤多，且明顯影響文意之表達。／劣（0分）＝全文文法錯誤嚴重，導致文意不明。
字彙、拼字：優（5-4分）＝用字精確、得宜，且幾無拼字、大小寫錯誤。／可（3分）＝字詞單調、重複，用字偶有不當，少許拼字、大小寫錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。／差（2-1分）＝用字、拼字、大小寫錯誤多，明顯影響文意之表達。／劣（0分）＝只寫出或抄襲與題意有關的零碎字詞。
（註：本「英文作文分項式評分標準」為 105 年 7 月修訂之版本。）

issues: 同年兩份參考試卷：units.json 的 ref-107 含兩份題本——paper-1.pdf「指定科目考試參考試卷（107學年度起適用）英文考科」與 paper-2.pdf「學科能力測驗參考試卷（107學年度起適用）英文考科」，依任務規則分別輸出 ref-107-a（指考參考試卷：paper-1.pdf、answer-1.pdf、考試說明 other-1.pdf）與 ref-107-b（學測參考試卷：paper-2.pdf、answer-2.pdf、考試說明 other-3.pdf）。other-1.pdf 與 other-2.pdf 是同一個檔案（md5 相同，皆為「107指考英文考試說明」），other-3.pdf 與 other-4.pdf 亦同（「107學測英文考試說明」），sources.other 兩個都列。

結構核對：本卷是指考參考試卷，對照 gsat-spec.json legacy_ast 期別「98–110」（本卷不屬學測期別）：詞彙題 1–10（各1分，題本標為「詞彙題」，與 spec 註記 107–110 題本稱「詞彙題」相符）、綜合測驗 11–20（2篇×5題，各1分）、文意選填 21–30（12個選項 A–L，各1分）、篇章結構 31–35（6個選項 A–F，各2分）、閱讀測驗 36–51（4篇×4題，各2分）、中譯英 2題各4分、英文作文 20分（至少120個單詞，文分兩段）；第壹部分單選題 72分＋第貳部分非選擇題 28分＝100分；考試時間 80分鐘（封面作答注意事項）；不倒扣（「答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算」，與 spec penalty_by_year 100–110 相同）。無差異。

題本誤植，照原文保留並在此註記：(a) 第40–43題的題組標示印成「第 40 至 44 題為題組」（group_label 照錄「第40至44題為題組」），實際此題組只有40–43四題，第44題屬於下一個「第 44 至 47 題為題組」；(b) 文意選填說明寫「請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (J) 選項中分別選出最適當者」，但選項庫實際有 (A)–(L) 12個選項（答案用到 K、L），說明照錄；(c) 第3題題號後少了句點（印成「3 Tom ______ …」），只影響題號，題幹不受影響；(d) 第4題空格為5個底線「_____」，其餘題目為6個，照錄。

格式與符號：第46題題幹「…supporting the web itself ?」問號前有空格，照原文保留。第49題選項中的箭號在 PDF 文字層是 Symbol 字型私用區字元（U+F0E0），依頁面影像轉成「→」。第39、42、45、51題題幹引號內的字詞在選文中以粗體標示（success is still a long shot、Peter Fabergé and his successors repeatedly met the challenge、so、that），題目不是問「畫底線的字」，依 schema 不保留格式；第48–51題選文中 Anopheles 為斜體，未保留。選文換行處的連字號（social-／network-style）依頁面影像判斷為複合詞本身的連字號，保留為 social-network-style。

答案來源：answer-1.pdf「大學入學考試中心 指定科目考試參考試卷 英文考科參考答案」——第1頁選擇題答案表（51題，pdftotext＋頁面影像逐題核對）、第2頁中譯英參考答案（大括號版面，看頁面影像轉寫）。本卷沒有評分原則檔、也沒有作文範文，sources.scoring 為空陣列，英文作文 answer 為 null。另以考試說明 other-1.pdf 試題舉例核對：第31–35題「參考答案：BEAFC」、第44–47題「BACB」、第48–51題「DBCB」，與 answer-1.pdf 一致。

中譯英：answer 取參考答案每個可替換位置的第一個寫法組成一句（可省略的小括號部分保留，food(s) 取 foods）；完整的可替換寫法以 {A | B} 記號逐字放在 scoring_notes。兩題的組合數分別達 6,912 與 3,888 種，第1題又有主詞單複數一致的限制（food is／contains、foods are／contain、substance that is、ingredients/elements that are），機械展開會產生不合文法的句子，所以不做完整展開；accepted_answers 只列出以 answer 為基準、每個位置各換一種寫法的句子（第1題18句、第2題15句；換成 food 單數時一併改 is／contains）。原版面 consider 後同樣標「(is/are)」可省略，accepted_answers 收 we consider safe 與 we consider are safe 兩種。

英文作文：scoring_notes 放考試說明 other-1.pdf 第13頁（PDF 第17頁）的「英文作文分項式評分標準」（105年7月修訂版），這是考試說明列出的通用標準，不是本題專屬的評分原則，已在 scoring_notes 開頭註明。題目要求文分兩段，tags.paragraphs=2；essay_type 用 topic（二選一說明理由的主題寫作，兩段落）。提示中的兩個產品說明框以 figures 描述並轉成 rows，框內文字也逐字收在 stem；PDF 文字層左右兩框逐行交錯，以頁面影像確認各框文字。
統計：參考試卷不是正式施測的考卷，大考中心沒有發布統計（units.json 也沒有 stats 檔），所有小題 stats 為 null、sources.stats 為空陣列；validator「整份考卷沒有任何統計資料」warning 屬預期。沿用題在原考試年度有統計，但那不是本試卷的數據，沒有搬過來（要用可依 reused_from 回查原卷）。
validator「題號重複 [1, 2]」warning 屬預期：中譯英兩題題本編為 1.、2.，英文作文沒有題號（no 填 1）；no 必須是整數，故沿用題本編號，以 label「中譯英1」「中譯英2」「英文作文」區分，label 無重複（同 ast-104、gsat-106 慣例）。

沿用歷屆試題：本卷全部由100–105學年度指考試題組成（考試說明 other-1.pdf 的試題舉例也標出第31–35題出自103學年度指考、第44–47題出自100學年度指考、第48–51題出自103學年度指考）。以擴充欄位 reused_from {exam, no} 標在小題上（同 ref-111、ref-115 慣例），有改動的另加 modified 說明。對應：1←ast-105第8題、2←ast-103第3題、3←ast-104第2題、4←ast-101第7題、5←ast-102第1題、6←ast-103第10題、7←ast-101第6題、8←ast-102第7題、9←ast-101第8題、10←ast-105第5題；11–15←ast-101第11–15題；16–20←ast-105第16–20題；21–30←ast-101第21–30題；31–35←ast-103第31–35題；36–39←ast-102第36–39題；40–43←ast-104第36–39題；44–47←ast-100第44–47題；48–51←ast-103第48–51題；中譯英1、2←ast-101中譯英1、2；英文作文←ast-102英文作文。以程式逐題比對原卷 pdftotext 文字（題幹、選項、選文、選項庫）並對照原卷答案檔：有改動的是第4題（題幹與選項順序）、第6題（一個選項）、第7題（選項順序）、第21–30題（選文刪去 processions and）、第39題（引號）、第44–47題（附圖改為灰階），細節見各題 reused_from.modified；其餘逐字相同（空格底線長度不同不計），答案以選項內容計全部與原卷相同。中譯英作答說明 ast-101 為「…並標明子題號（1、2）。」，本卷為「…並標明子題號。」；英文作文提示 ast-102 用「提示：」，本卷用「提示︰」，其餘文字相同。
